neighbours.label: an idealising assumption in a scientific model (perfect markets, freely combining, constant random motion)
fire: The textbook model assumes perfect competition, with many buyers and sellers.
In an ideal gas the molecules move freely and never attract each other.
Economists often assume frictionless markets where prices adjust instantly.
Under perfect information every trader knows the true value of the asset.
The genes are assumed to assort freely when they lie on different chromosomes.
In the model, the particles are in constant random motion and collide elastically.
Assume the two liquids mix perfectly and reach equilibrium at once.
With perfectly flexible wages, unemployment would disappear in the long run.
quiet: The textbook describes how many buyers and sellers trade in local markets.
In the tank the gas molecules were measured at room temperature.
Economists collected data on prices in markets across the country.
Every trader at the firm studies the history of the asset carefully.
The genes lie on different chromosomes in most of these species.
In the lab, the particles were filmed with a high-speed camera.
Pour the two liquids into the beaker and stir them with a rod.
When wages rose last year, unemployment fell in several regions.

notes: Card: peaks on ' perfect' financial markets, ' freely' combinable, 'are| in constant random motion', 'would be| if all ...'; reversed output promotes ' freely', ' perfect', ' equilibrium', ' rapid', ' mixing'.
